findings.F1: Calmar fails because the falls are long and come with bear markets in the coins: the yearly return is 22.4 % against a deepest fall of 33.3 %. That fall took 226 days to its trough, from w1 to w3, while holding the coins lost 64 %. The next falls are 27.7 % (w16–w17, coins −44 %), 25.8 % (w12–w15, coins −76 %) and 23.1 % (w18–w21, coins −26 %).
findings.F2: The book loses in the windows where the coins fall: w2 −10.7 % (coins −44 %), w3 −16.6 %, w13 −9.5 % (coins −34 %), w14 −8.1 % (coins −49 %), w18 −14.5 % (coins −22 %). It is long in bear markets, with only the 60-day filter between it and them.
findings.F3: Held positions earn nothing once the coin has turned down, even with the 60-day return positive at entry. The daily gain on held bars is −3.0 bps (t −0.63, 1144 bars) when the coin's 20-day return is below −6 %, and +6.2 bps (t 0.69) between −6 % and +2 %. It is +28 to +38 bps (t 2.7 to 3.1) above +2 %.
findings.F4: The same split appears against the 50-day average, measured as the share the close sits above or below it. Held bars earn −7.5 bps (t −0.66, 791 bars) with the close more than 2 % below it, and +8.6 bps (t 1.10) within −2 % to +5 %. They earn +31 to +41 bps (t 2.6 to 3.1) above +5 %.
findings.F5: Held bars also earn nothing at the weak end of the 60-day return. Below +3 % they earn −3.6 bps (t −0.33). Between +3 % and +47 % they earn +32 to +44 bps (t 2.0 to 3.2).
findings.F6: The 10-day run-up the idea grades by does not grade the trades: mean net gain per trade by run-up quartile is 2.2 %, 3.1 %, 2.0 % and 3.8 % (452 trades each).
findings.F7: Calm, contracting volatility carries no gain. Held bars where the coin's 10-day volatility is below 0.65 of its 60-day volatility earn +4.6 bps (t 0.54, 666 bars). Above 1.27 of it they earn +53.6 bps (t 2.55).
findings.F8: Cost is not the cause. The unusual move per case (+0.44 %, 1205 cases, t 1.28) is 2.3 times the 0.19 % cost of a trade, and the total move (+1.02 %) is 5.3 times it.

ideas.idea: When a coin closes above a price where it turned down several times in the past 90 days, it tends to keep rising over the next 5 days, only while its 60-day return is positive and its close is above its 50-day average, and the further its close stands above that average, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A break of a repeatedly held level is a reason to buy only when the coin already trades well above its 50-day average; a break made from below or near that average, as in the bear phases that carry the book's deepest falls, is a reason to stay out.
ideas.name: breakout above rising average

ideas.idea: When a coin closes above a price where it turned down several times in the past 90 days, it tends to keep rising over the next 5 days, only while its 60-day return is positive, and the larger its 20-day return before the break, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A break that comes after a strong month is a reason to buy; a break after a flat or falling month, which is where the held positions earned nothing, is a reason to refuse it.
ideas.name: breakout after strong month

ideas.idea: When a coin closes above a price where it turned down several times in the past 90 days, it tends to keep rising over the next 5 days, only while its 60-day return is positive, and the larger its 10-day volatility relative to its 60-day volatility, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A break that comes with widening daily swings is a reason to buy; a break in a quiet, contracting market is not.
ideas.name: breakout with expanding volatility
